statements.claim: The war was over when Ashvatthama, Drona's son, slipped into the sleeping Pandava camp by night and killed Draupadi's sons where they lay.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.7.12-13 (pack): after the heroes of the Kurus and Srinjayas fell in battle, Drauni, seeking his master's pleasure, cut off the heads of the sleeping sons of Krishnaa (Draupadi) — kṛṣṇāsutānāṃ svapatāṃ śirāṃsi.

statements.claim: Draupadi heard of the death of her sons and grieved; Krishna went to her and comforted her.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.7.14-16 (pack): the mother, hearing the ghastly slaughter of her sons, grieved terribly; Krishna consoled her with gentle words.

statements.claim: Krishna promised to wipe away her sorrow with the head of that unworthy son of a brahmin, the assailant who struck without warning.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.7.15 (pack): 'I will wipe away this sorrow of yours, good lady, with the head of the brahma-bandhu, the assailant' (yad brahmabandhoḥ śira ātatāyinaḥ); matches pack excerpt.

statements.claim: Arjuna took up the pursuit at once, Krishna himself driving his chariot.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.7.16-17 (pack): Arjuna is acyutamitra-sūtaḥ — he whose friend and charioteer is Acyuta (Krishna) — and the chase is by chariot.

statements.claim: The chase ran long and the horses were failing when Arjuna saw Ashvatthama stop and turn to face him.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.7.17-18 (pack): seeing him rushing from afar, Arjuna found himself without refuge, his horses spent (śrāntavājinam).

statements.claim: Ashvatthama, Drona's son schooled in the secret science of weapons, released a weapon no arrow could answer; a terrible fire blazed up in every direction, filling the sky from horizon to horizon.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.7.19-20 (pack): touching water, he released it, and a fierce tejas blazed in all directions; pack summary: 'After Ashvatthama releases the Brahmashira weapon... a terrified Arjuna calls on Krishna'.

statements.claim: Arjuna cried out to Krishna as mighty-armed, giver of fearlessness to devotees, the rescue of those being burned, naming him the primal person, the Lord beyond nature, who deludes the living world by his power of illusion and descended to lift the earth's burden; 'What is this, and from where does it come? O God of gods, I do not know.'
statements.evidence: BhP 1.7.21-25 (pack): 'Krishna, Krishna, mighty-armed one, giver of fearlessness to your devotees, you alone are the rescue of those being burned'; tvam ādyaḥ puruṣaḥ sākṣād īśvaraḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ... māyā... bhuvo bhārajihīrṣayā; 'kim idaṃ svit kuto veti devadeva na vedmy aham'.

statements.claim: Krishna answered: 'Know this to be the brahma weapon of Drona's son. He does not know how to recall it. Only an astra can quell an astra.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt rendering of BhP 1.7.26-27; Sanskrit verse 27: na hy asyānyatamaṃ kiñcid astraṃ pratyavakarśanam.

statements.claim: Arjuna, touching water as the rite requires, discharged his own weapon; the two fires met wrapped in a storm of arrows and together blazed so that the three worlds stood in peril.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'Arjuna discharges it'; BhP 1.7.29-30 (pack): saṃhatyānyonyam ubhayos tejasī śarasaṃvṛte; 'trīl lokān pradahan mahat' — burning the three worlds.

statements.claim: At Krishna's word Arjuna withdrew both weapons — his own and the one loosed against him — and the fires sank.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'at Krishna's word, withdraws both blazing weapons to save the worlds'; BhP 1.7.31 (pack) continues the account of the worlds' peril being averted.

statements.claim: 'In the camp behind him a mother still wept, and a promise still waited to be kept.' (closing frame)
statements.evidence: Connective echo of Draupadi's grief and Krishna's promise; not a discrete sourceable event.

notes: Faithful rendering of BhP 1.7.12-31. 'Meaning to do what would please his master' matches bhartuḥ priyaṃ (1.7.13). No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims found.

statements.claim: Ashvatthama was brought in bound — led with a rope, dragged like an animal, his face averted — and the man who had captured him looked away in disgust.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.7.32-33, 41 (pack): bound with a rope (rajjvā baddhvā), brought like an animal, face downward (paśuvat pāśabaddham avāṅmukham), by one disgusted with the deed (karmajugupsitena).

statements.claim: Bhima cried out not to spare him: 'This unworthy son of a brahmin — kill him! For what is he but the kind of man who would strike the mad, the careless, the sleeping, children, women, the helpless — who feeds his own life on the lives of others?'
statements.evidence: BhP 1.7.34-36 (pack): mainaṃ pārthārhasi trātuṃ brahmabandhum imaṃ jahi; mattaṃ pramattam unmattaṃ suptaṃ bālaṃ striyaṃ jaḍam; svaprāṇān yaḥ paraprāṇaiḥ prapuṣṇāti.

statements.claim: Bhima recalled the promise: 'You swore to Panchali that you would bring his head... I was listening when you swore it. Let this sinner die — this assailant, this slayer of his own kindred.'
statements.evidence: BhP 1.7.37-38 (pack): pratiśrutaṃ ca bhavatā pāñcālyai śṛṇvato mama... vadhyatāṃ pāpa ātatāyy ātmabandhuhā.

statements.claim: Draupadi could not bear the sight of him bound and dragged; she pleaded that Drona had been master of the secret science of weapons with its discharge and recall, that the blessed teacher lived on in his son, that his family be honored, and that his mother Gautami, devoted to her husband, not weep.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.7.42-46 (pack): satī, unable to bear his binding and leading (asahantyā bandhanānayanaṃ), speaks — sarahasyo dhanurvedaḥ savisargopasaṃyamaḥ; sa eṣa bhagavān droṇaḥ prajārūpeṇa vartate; mā rodīd asya jananī gautamī patidevatā.

statements.claim: Nakula and Sahadeva stood by, Satyaki and Arjuna waited, and Bhima, still burning, insisted that for such a man death itself was the only mercy.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.7.49-50 (pack): nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca yuyudhāno dhanañjayaḥ; tatrāha marṣito bhīmas tasya śreyān vadhaḥ smṛtaḥ.

statements.claim: Krishna, the four-armed one, heard Bhima's words and Draupadi's and gave judgment: 'A brahmin's unworthy son is not to be slain, yet an assailant deserves punishment. Both are my ordinances; uphold them. Keep the promise you made to your beloved, and satisfy Bhima, Panchali, and me.'
statements.evidence: BhP 1.7.51-54 (pack): niśamya bhīmagaditaṃ draupadyāś ca caturbhujaḥ; excerpt renders Krishna's speech (verses 52-54); kuru pratiśrutaṃ satyaṃ yat tat sāntvayatā priyām.

statements.claim: Arjuna, understanding Krishna's heart, cut the jewel away from the head of Drona's son — the jewel along with the hair — then released him from his bonds and drove him from the camp.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Then Arjuna, understanding Krishna's heart, cut off the jewel along with the hair of the brahmin, released him from his bonds, and drove him from the camp'; BhP 1.7.55-56: vapanaṃ draviṇādānaṃ sthānān niryāpaṇaṃ tathā.

statements.claim: 'The splendor of the child-killer was gone, struck down — as the old tellers would say — by the very children he had killed.'
statements.evidence: Poetic gloss, explicitly framed as a teller's phrase, on bālahatyāhataprabham (1.7.55: his splendor destroyed by the child-slaying).

statements.claim: The vow was kept 'in the only way that could keep them all: a punishment that took everything but life.'
statements.evidence: Interpretive summary of the jewel-shaving-banishment judgment (1.7.55-56); framing, not a new factual assertion.

notes: Speech order (Bhima → Draupadi → Bhima's 'death is better' → Krishna) matches BhP 1.7.34-56. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims found.

statements.claim: Bhishma lay on his bed of arrows and would not die until the sun entered the northern course — the auspicious solstice.
statements.evidence: Pack index summary: 'Lying on his bed of arrows at the auspicious northern solstice, Bhishma fixes his gaze on Krishna standing before him'; BhP 1.9.28: the awaited time (sa kālaḥ) arrived while he spoke.

statements.claim: He had fallen in the war and, still living after it ended, waited, taught, and watched the sky as survivors came and sat by him.
statements.evidence: Scene-setting consistent with the pack (he is alive on the field after the war, teaching until his hour comes, 1.9.25-28); 'the war he had foreseen and refused to leave' is connective framing.

statements.claim: Bhishma said of Krishna's coming: 'the compassion of the Lord toward his unalloyed devotees. This very Krishna has come to me as I give up my life... May he be my refuge.'
statements.evidence: BhP 1.9.21 (pack): tathāpy ekānta-bhakteṣu paśya bhūpānukampitam; pack excerpt: 'This very Krishna, who came to me as I give up my life, out of love for his unalloyed devotees — may he be my refuge.'

statements.claim: He asked that the Lord wait while he gave up the body, his mind merged in him with devotion and his voice chanting his name.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.9.22-23 (pack): bhaktyāveśya mano yasmin vācā yannāma kīrtayan; sa devadevo bhagavān pratīkṣatāṃ kalevaraṃ yāvad idaṃ hinomy aham.

statements.claim: With the Pandavas and gathered sages looking on, he taught the duties of charity, of kings, of those seeking release, and the four ends of human life, each with its means, according to rank and stage.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.9.25-27 (pack): dānadharmān rājadharmān mokṣadharmān vibhāgaśaḥ; dharmārthakāmamokṣāṃś ca sahopāyān yathāvarṇaṃ yathāśramam.

statements.claim: While he spoke, the hour he had waited for came.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.9.28 (pack): dharmaṃ pravadatas tasya sa kālaḥ pratyupasthitaḥ.

statements.claim: Gathering in his speech, he fixed his unblinking gaze on the four-armed Krishna standing before him in yellow robes, and offered his final praise: 'May my love rest on Krishna.'
statements.evidence: BhP 1.9.29, 31-32 (pack): tadopasaṃhṛtya giraḥ... ; pack excerpt: 'he fixed his unblinking gaze upon the four-armed Krishna standing before him in yellow robes, and offered his final praise: May my love rest on Krishna'; tribhuvanakamanaṃ tamālavarṇaṃ ravikara-gaura-varāmbara dadhāne.

statements.claim: He remembered Krishna dark as the tamala tree with garments bright as the rays of the sun, driving the chariot through battlefield dust with locks disheveled and sweat on his face.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.9.32-33 (pack): tamālavarṇaṃ ravikara-gaura-varāmbara; turagarajo-vidhūmra-viṣvak kacalulita-śramavāry-alaṅkṛtāsye.

statements.claim: He remembered how Krishna placed the chariot between the two armies and, hearing his friend's plea, set aside his own word — Krishna, who had sworn he would not fight — and leapt down to make true the vow of the old warrior, his armor shattered by sharp arrows and bathed in blood, glorious to behold.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.9.34-38 (pack): sapadi sakhivaco niśamya madhye nija-parayor balayo rathaṃ niveśya; svanigamam apahāya matpratijñām ṛtam adhikartum avapluto rathasthaḥ; śitaviśikhahato viśīrṇadaṃśaḥ kṣatajaparipluta ātatāyino me; tac chriyekṣaṇīye.

statements.claim: He remembered the assembly at Yudhishthira's Rajasuya, crowded with sages and kings, where Krishna moved with gentle smile and loving glance.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.9.39-40 (pack): lalita-gati-vilāsa-valguhāsa-praṇaya-nirīkṣaṇa-...; munigaṇa-nṛpavarya-saṅkule 'ntaḥ sadasi yudhiṣṭhira-rājasūya eṣām.

statements.claim: 'Him, the unborn, dwelling in the heart of every embodied being — on him let my love rest.'
statements.evidence: BhP 1.9.41 (pack): tam imam aham ajam śarīrabhājāṃ hṛdi hṛdi dhiṣṭhitam.

statements.claim: With pure concentration, his mind freed from attachment and fixed on the Primal Person, his sins burned away by that one sight, the weariness of a hundred wounds fell from him.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.9.30 (pack): viśuddhayā dhāraṇayā hatāśubhas tadīkṣayaivāśu gatāyudhaśramaḥ ('his evils destroyed by that very look, the weariness of weapons quickly gone'); 'a hundred wounds' is a rhetorical rendering of the weapon-weariness.

statements.claim: The sages knew Bhishma was merging into the attributeless Brahman; drums sounded, played by gods and men together; and the rites for the departed were performed.
statements.evidence: BhP 1.9.43-45 (pack): sampadyamānam ājñāya bhīṣmaṃ brahmaṇi niṣkale; tatra dundubhayo nedur devamānavavāditāḥ; tasya nirharaṇādīni samparetasya.

notes: Whole scene (BhP 1.9.21-45) rendered closely; 'yellow robes' matches the pack's own excerpt wording. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims found.

statements.claim: Uddhava, speaking long afterward of Krishna's deeds, recalled the field at Kurukshetra.
statements.evidence: Pack source is Uddhava's discourse (BhP 3.3, 'Uddhava said...'), recalling the war after the fact.

statements.claim: Uddhava had been Krishna's companion and messenger across the years, carrying the Lord's words from court to court.
statements.evidence: Background characterization of Uddhava's role; not asserted in the pack excerpts (BhP 3.3.11-12).

statements.claim: The earth trembled at Kurukshetra beneath the armies of the cousins — the sons of two brothers — the kings of the land ranged on either side.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'The earth trembled at Kurukshetra beneath the armies of the kings who fell on either side' (BhP 3.3.11-12); Pandavas and Kauravas are sons of the brothers Pandu and Dhritarashtra.

statements.claim: The field grew dark with men, horses and raised standards; the earth beneath seemed to know what was coming.
statements.evidence: Connective elaboration of the trembling; no discrete sourceable assertion.

statements.claim: The burden that had pressed on the earth was lifted at Kurukshetra, and that was Krishna's design — the war was his instrument and the earth would be lighter when it was done.
statements.evidence: Pack index summary: 'the burden of the earth lifted by Krishna's design'; consistent with the corpus theme of the Lord's descent to lift the earth's burden (cf. BhP 1.7.24).

statements.claim: The kings fell on either side, so many that the field seemed to be made of them; every house had sent its sons and every kingdom its king.
statements.evidence: Core fact (kings of both sides fallen, patitān nṛpān, BhP 3.3.11) supported; the hyperbole is connective.

statements.claim: Karna, Dushasana and Shakuni — those who had counseled the ruin — were destroyed in fortune and in life by the ripening of their own evil counsel.
statements.evidence: BhP 3.3.12 (pack): karṇa-duḥśāsana-saubalānāṃ kumantra-pākena hata-śriyāyuṣam (Saubala = Shakuni, son of Subala).

statements.claim: At the last, Duryodhana himself, Suyodhana, lay on the field with his thigh broken and his followers fallen about him, and the cousins' quarrel was ended.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'Suyodhana, with his followers, lying with his thigh broken' (BhP 3.3.11-12); Suyodhana is another name for Duryodhana.

statements.claim: Uddhava, telling of it, did not rejoice and never spoke of that field as a victory.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'he did not rejoice to see' (BhP 3.3.11-12); pack summary: no triumph in the memory.

statements.claim: Closing reflections: the quiet had cost more than anyone who had called for the war had imagined paying.
statements.evidence: Interpretive coda on Uddhava's non-rejoicing; connective.

notes: Duryodhana's thigh-broken fall and Karna/Dushasana/Shakuni's ruin by their own counsel map directly to BhP 3.3.11-12. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims found.

statements.claim: At Upaplavya, after hearing Krishna's account of the failed peace in the court of the Kurus, Yudhishthira addressed his brothers in Krishna's presence.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.151 (pack): 'king Yudhishthira the Just... addressed his brothers in the presence of Kesava and said, Ye have heard all that had happened in the court of the assembled Kurus'; pack index location: Upaplavya.

statements.claim: Seven Akshauhinis of troops stood ready, and seven celebrated warriors would lead them: Drupada, Virata, Dhrishtadyumna, Sikhandin, Satyaki, Chekitana and Bhimasena of great energy — all conversant with the Vedas, practised in vows, versed in policy and accomplished in war.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.151 (pack): 'Here are seven Akshauhinis of troops... They are Drupada, and Virata, and Dhristadyumna, and Sikhandin, and Satyaki, Chekitana, and Bhimasena of great energy... conversant with the Vedas... practised excellent vows... conversant with policy, and accomplished in war.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira asked who might become the leader of the seven and withstand in battle Bhishma, 'who is like unto a fire having arrows for its flames.'
statements.evidence: MBh 5.151 (pack): 'who that warrior is conversant with all kinds of battle-array, that may become the leader of these seven and may also withstand in battle Bhishma who is like unto a fire having arrows for its flames.'

statements.claim: Sahadeva named Virata, the king of the Matsyas — closely related, sympathising in distress, endued with great might, skilled in weapons, irresistible — relying on whom they hoped to recover their share of the kingdom; he would bear in battle both Bhishma and the mighty car-warriors.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.151 (pack), Sahadeva's speech: 'Closely related to us, sympathising with us in our distress, endued with great might... the mighty king of the Matsyas, Virata, relying upon whom we hope to recover our share of the kingdom, will be able to bear in battle both Bhishma and all those mighty car-warriors.'

statements.claim: Nakula named Drupada, their father-in-law — respectable in years, scripture and birth; he had studied the science of weapons with the sage Bharadwaja; he always challenged Drona and mighty Bhishma; he had once performed, moved by wrath with his wife, the austerest penance for the destruction of Drona; he cherished them like a father and would withstand both Drona and Bhishma rushing to battle.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.151 (pack), Nakula's speech: 'he that studied the science of weapons (with the sage Bharadwaja)... always challenges Drona and mighty Bhishma... with his wife, performed, moved by wrath, the austerest of penances for the destruction of Drona... that bull among monarchs who always cherishes us like a father... will be able to withstand both Drona and Bhishma rushing to battle.'

statements.claim: Arjuna described Dhrishtadyumna: sprung into life through the power of ascetic penances and the gratification of sages; issued from the sacrificial fire-hole armed with bow and sword, accoutred in armour of steel, mounted on a car with excellent steeds, the clatter of his wheels deep as the roar of clouds; lion-like in frame and voice; incapable of being penetrated by weapons; like an elephant with rent temples; truthful in speech, his passions under control; born for the destruction of Drona.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.151 (pack), Arjuna's speech: 'sprang into life through the power of ascetic penances and the gratification of sages; who issued from the sacrificial fire-hole armed with bow and sword... the clatter of whose car-wheels was as deep as the roar of mighty masses of clouds; resembling the very lion in his frame... incapable of being penetrated by weapons of any kind... looks like an elephant with rent temples; this Dhrishtadyumna, truthful in speech, and with passions under control, was born for the destruction of Drona.'

statements.claim: Arjuna said he saw no man except Dhrishtadyumna able to withstand Bhishma of great vows, whose arrows strike with the vehemence of the thunderbolt and fall like flames of fire.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.151 (pack): 'able to bear Bhishma's arrows which strike with the vehemence of the thunderbolt... and fall like flames of fire... I do not, O king, see the man except Dhrishtadyumna, who is able to withstand Bhishma of great vows.'

statements.claim: Krishna, the lotus-eyed one, looking toward Arjuna, said he fully approved all the warriors named and named Dhrishtadyumna as the leader.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (MBh 5.151): 'the lotus-eyed Krishna said, eyeing Dhananjaya, the while, O king, I fully approve of all those powerful warriors whom ye have named for becoming the leaders of thy troops... As regards our leader, I would name that chastiser of foes, Dhrishtadyumna.'

statements.claim: The fire-born prince of Panchala would stand at the head of the seven divisions, and the purpose for which the sages said he was born would meet him on the field.
statements.evidence: Foreshadowing coda; the fire-birth and 'born for the destruction of Drona' are supported (5.151), the on-field meeting is connective.

notes: Very close to Ganguli 5.151; speeches are attributed to the same speakers (Sahadeva, Nakula, Arjuna) and order preserved. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims found.

statements.claim: Yudhishthira had marched out desiring battle and encamped on Kurukshetra, protected by Vasudeva, aided by Virata and Drupada with their sons, surrounded by the Kekayas, the Vrishnis and other kings by hundreds, watched over by mighty car-warriors, like Indra surrounded by the Adityas.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.154 (pack), Janamejaya's question: 'Yudhishthira had, with his troops marched from the desire of battle and encamped on Kurukshetra, protected by Vasudeva, and aided by Virata and Drupada with their sons, and surrounded by the Kekayas, the Vrishnis, and other kings by hundreds, and watched over by numerous mighty car-warriors, like the great Indra himself by the Adityas.'

statements.claim: Calling Karna, Dussasana and Sakuni, Duryodhana declared that Kesava had gone to the sons of Pritha without achieving his object and, filled with wrath, would surely stimulate the Pandavas; that a battle between himself and the Pandavas was much desired by Vasudeva; that Bhimasena and Arjuna were ever of one mind with Krishna and Yudhishthira much under Bhimasena's influence; that Virata and Drupada, against whom he had waged hostilities, had both become leaders of Yudhishthira's host; and that the battle would be fierce and terrific — so all sloth should be cast off and every preparation made.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.154 (pack), Duryodhana's speech: 'Kesava hath gone to the sons of Pritha, without having been able to achieve his object. Filled with wrath as he is, he will surely stimulate the Pandavas. A battle between myself and Pandavas is much desired by Vasudeva. Bhimasena and Arjuna are ever of the same mind with him. Yudhishthira, again, is very much under the influence of Bhimasena. Virata and Drupada whom I had waged hostilities with... both of them have become the leaders of Yudhishthira's host. The battle, therefore, that will take place, will be a fierce and terrific one. Casting off all sloth, cause every preparation to be made for the encounter.'

statements.claim: His orders: allied kings were to pitch spacious tents by hundreds and thousands on Kurukshetra, near water and fuel, in positions where the foe could never stop the supply roads; the road from the city to the camp was to be levelled; and it was to be proclaimed that very day that the march would commence the next day.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.154 (pack): 'Let the kings (my allies) pitch their tents by hundreds and thousands on Kurukshetra, all of which must be spacious... near enough to places abounding with water and fuel, in such positions that the communications thereto for sending supplies may not be stopped... Let the road from our city to the camp be made level... Let it be proclaimed this very day... that our march will commence tomorrow.'

statements.claim: The monarchs rose from their costly seats with wrath, rubbed their mace-like arms blazing with gold bracelets and decked with sandal paste, donned head-gears, garments and ornaments; car-warriors furnished the cars, horse-experts harnessed the steeds, elephant-experts equipped the elephants, and foot-soldiers took up arms and gold-decorated armour; filled with rejoicing millions, the city of Duryodhana wore the bright aspect of a festive occasion.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.154 (pack): 'all those monarchs... rose up from their costly seats, with wrath having the foe for its objects... rub their mace-like arms, blazing with bracelets of gold, and decked with the paste of sandal... wear their head-gears and lower and upper garments... car-warriors began to superintend the furnishing of their cars... harness their steeds... equip those huge animals... foot-soldiers began to take up various kinds of arms and case their bodies in... armour decorated with gold... the city of Duryodhana then, filled as it was with rejoicing millions, wore the bright aspect of a festive occasion.'

statements.claim: At the prospect of battle the Kuru capital looked like the ocean at the appearance of the moon — crowds its waters, cars-elephants-horses its fishes, conchs and drums its roar, bright weapons its white foam, rows of houses the mountains on its beach.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.154 (pack): 'the Kuru capital at the prospect of battle looked like the ocean on the appearance of the moon... the vast crowds of humanity representing its waters... cars, elephants, and horses representing its fishes; the tumult of conchs and drums, its roar; ...the bright weapons its white foam; the rows of houses the mountains on its beach.'

statements.claim: Krishna had gone to the Kuru court with words of peace and the prince of the Kurus had met them with deceit; pressed by Yudhishthira, Krishna answered in a voice deep as that of the clouds or cymbals: 'That wicked-souled wight beareth no good will towards thee... we do not desire to make peace with the Kauravas by abandoning our property. War, therefore, is that which should now take place.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (MBh 5.154): 'Krishna replied, in a voice deep as that of the clouds or cymbals... That wicked-souled wight beareth no good will towards thee... As regards ourselves, we do not desire to make peace with the Kauravas by abandoning our property. War, therefore, is that which should now take place.'

statements.claim: 'Two decisions, made on opposite sides of Kurukshetra, now faced each other across the field.' (closing bridge)
statements.evidence: Compression of the Kuru capital's war-readiness and the Pandava camp's resolve into one image; evocative framing, no factual assertion.

notes: Both halves of the story (Duryodhana's preparations in 5.154 and Krishna's war declaration in the pack excerpt) are supported nearly verbatim. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims found.

statements.claim: Recollecting the words Vasudeva had spoken, Yudhishthira pressed Krishna once more, reminding him that he knew the views of Duryodhana, Karna and Sakuni the son of Suvala, the views of the Pandavas, the words of Vidura and Bhishma, and the words of wisdom spoken by Kunti, and asked him to say, after reflection and without hesitation, what was for their good.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.155 (pack): 'Recollecting the words spoken by Vasudeva, Yudhishthira once more addressed that scion of Vrishni's race... Thou, O Vasudeva, art acquainted with the views of Duryodhana, Karna, and Sakuni, the son of Suvala... Thou hast heard the words uttered by both Vidura and Bhishma... the words of wisdom spoken by Kunti. Overlooking all these, tell us... without hesitation, what is for our good.'

statements.claim: Krishna answered in a voice deep as that of the clouds or cymbals: his words in the Kuru court, consistent with both virtue and profit, had found no response in Duryodhana, in whom deceit supplied the place of wisdom.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.155 (pack): 'Krishna replied, in a voice deep as that of the clouds or cymbals... consistent with both virtue and profit, those words that were uttered by me in the Kuru court found no response in the Kuru prince Duryodhana with whom deceit supplieth the place of wisdom.'

statements.claim: Krishna said Duryodhana listened not to the counsels of Bhishma, Vidura or Krishna himself; transgressed everybody; wished neither virtue nor fame; relying on Karna regarded everything as already won; had even ordered Krishna's incarceration without obtaining the fruition of that wish; neither Bhishma nor Drona said anything on the subject; and all of them followed Duryodhana except Vidura.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.155 (pack): 'That wretch of wicked understanding listeneth not in the least to the counsels of Bhishma or Vidura or mine... Suyodhana of wicked heart... even ordered my incarceration but he did not, however, obtain the fruition of that wish. Neither Bhishma nor Drona said anything on that subject. Indeed, all of them follow Duryodhana, except Vidura.'

statements.claim: Sakuni, Karna and Dussasana, all equally foolish, had given foolish and vindictive Duryodhana much improper advice regarding the Pandavas.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.155 (pack): 'Sakuni, the son of Suvala, and Karna, and Dussasana, all equally foolish, gave foolish and vindictive Duryodhana much improper advice regarding thee.'

statements.claim: Krishna concluded: that wicked-souled wight bore no good will towards Yudhishthira; not even all the kings of his army together held the sinfulness that resided in Duryodhana alone; the Pandavas did not desire peace with the Kauravas by abandoning their property; war, therefore, should now take place.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.155 (pack): 'that wicked-souled wight beareth no good will towards thee. Not even in all these kings together, that form thy army, is that measure of sinfulness and wickedness which resideth in Duryodhana alone. As regards ourselves, we do not desire to make peace with the Kauravas by abandoning our property. War, therefore, is that which should now take place.'

statements.claim: All the kings present looked at Yudhishthira's face; understanding their intention, Yudhishthira with Bhima, Arjuna and the twins gave the word to draw up the troops in battle array; a great uproar rose among the Pandava host and the soldiers were filled with joy.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.155 (pack): 'all the kings (there present)... without saying anything, looked at Yudhishthira's face. And Yudhishthira, understanding the intention of those monarchs, said, with Bhima and Arjuna and the twins, Draw up the troops in battle array... a great uproar rose amongst the Pandava army and all the soldiers were filled with joy.'

statements.claim: Yudhishthira, beholding the impending slaughter of those who deserved not to be slain, sighed deeply and lamented that the calamity for which he had accepted exile into the woods and suffered so much misery overtook them of a set purpose, asking how they could fight reverend superiors whom they could on no account slay and what victory was to be won by slaying preceptors of venerable age.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.155 (pack): 'King Yudhishthira the Just, however, beholding the (impending) slaughter of those that deserved not to be slain, began to sigh deeply... That for the sake of which I accepted an exile into the woods... that great calamity overtaketh us of a set purpose... How shall we fight with those reverend superiors (of ours) whom we on no account can slay? What kind of victory shall we achieve by slaying our preceptors of venerable age?'

statements.claim: Arjuna repeated to his elder brother all the words Krishna had said, noting Yudhishthira had understood the words of Kunti and Vidura repeated to him by Devaki's son, that neither Vidura nor Kunti would say anything sinful, and that they could not withdraw without engaging in battle; Krishna confirmed to Arjuna, 'It is even so.'
statements.evidence: MBh 5.155 (pack): 'Savyasachin repeated to his elder brother all those words that Vasudeva had said... Thou hast... certainly understood all the words spoken by Kunti and Vidura, that were repeated to thee by Devaki's son... neither Vidura nor Kunti would say anything that is sinful. Besides this... we cannot withdraw without engaging in battle... Vasudeva also said unto Partha, It is even so (as thou hast said).'

statements.claim: That night the sons of Pandu made up their minds for war and passed the hours with their soldiers in great happiness.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.155 (pack): 'The sons of Pandu then... made up their minds for war, and passed that night with their soldiers in great happiness.'

statements.claim: Handsome Janardana, endued with great intelligence, the younger brother of Sankarshana, was chosen as the guide of Arjuna and the driver of his steeds.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (MBh 5.155): 'And handsome Janardana endued with great intelligence, he who was the younger brother of Sankarshana, was chosen as the guide of Arjuna and the driver of his steeds.'

statements.claim: 'The counsellor of the war would now drive the chariot into it, and the friend who had carried the words of peace would stand closest to the man who had to fight.'
statements.evidence: Connective closing gloss on Krishna's new role as charioteer.

notes: Nearly verbatim to Ganguli 5.155 including direct speech. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims found.

statements.claim: While the Pandava camp rang with the order to draw up for battle, one man among the Vrishnis would take no part in it — Krishna's own elder brother, Balarama.
statements.evidence: The draw-up order is in MBh 5.155 (pack passage); that Krishna is the younger brother of Sankarshana (= Balarama) is in the pack excerpt, making Balarama his elder; Balarama's refusal/departure is the pack's subject (excerpt + index summary).

statements.claim: All the kings had looked at Yudhishthira's face; Yudhishthira, understanding, gave the word with Bhima, Arjuna and the twins to draw up the troops; a great uproar rose and the soldiers were filled with joy; but Yudhishthira sighed deeply over the impending slaughter of those undeserving of death, recalling the exile and misery he had borne for the sake of that calamity and asking how they could fight their reverend superiors.
statements.evidence: MBh 5.155 (pack passage): identical to the scene in the pack — 'all the kings... looked at Yudhishthira's face... said, with Bhima and Arjuna and the twins, Draw up the troops in battle array... King Yudhishthira the Just, however... began to sigh deeply... How shall we fight with those reverend superiors (of ours) whom we on no account can slay?'

statements.claim: Balarama was unwilling to fight against either the Pandavas or Duryodhana; both armies held men he had known all his life, and he would raise his arm against neither.
statements.evidence: Pack index summary: 'Balarama, unwilling to fight against either the Pandavas or Duryodhana'; the kinship rationale is connective elaboration consistent with it.

statements.claim: Balarama declared: 'As regards myself, I dare not cast my eyes on the world without Krishna on my side. It is for this that I follow whatever Krishna seeketh to achieve.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (MBh 5.155): 'As regards myself, I dare not cast my eyes on the world without Krishna (on my side). It is for this that I follow whatever Krishna seeketh to achieve.'

statements.claim: Balarama said he would repair to the tirtha of the Saraswati for ablutions, for he could not behold with indifference the destruction of the Kauravas.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (MBh 5.155): 'I shall now repair to the tirtha of the Saraswati for ablutions, for I shall not be able to behold with indifference the destruction of the Kauravas.'

statements.claim: He walked to the Saraswati, the sacred river of the sages, to its holy fords — places of ablution and prayer where pilgrims came to be cleansed.
statements.evidence: Descriptive expansion of 'the tirtha of the Saraswati for ablutions' (pack excerpt); atmosphere, not a new sourceable event.

statements.claim: Closing reflections: a warrior leaving a war he could neither join nor watch, choosing the side of neither army and the one cause he could not abandon.
statements.evidence: Interpretive coda on the pack's summary ('follows Krishna's cause but departs rather than watch the Kauravas' destruction').

notes: Balarama's two quoted speeches match the pack excerpt verbatim. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED claims found.
